description:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: How Men and Women Rank Benefit Importance as a Tradeoff to Earnings
TEXT IN IMAGE:
Legend: Women, Men
Y-axis categories (top to bottom):
- Better health, dental, and vision insurance
- Work-from-home options
- More flexible hours
- Unlimited vacation
- More vacation time
- Paid maternity/paternity leave
- Student loan assistance
- Free day-care services
- Tuition assistance
- Free fitness/yoga classes
- Free gym membership
- Free coffee
- Free snacks
- Company-wide retreats
- Team bonding events
- Weekly free employee outings
- On-site gym
X-axis label: Percentage ranking highly influential
Data labels (Women / Men):
- Better health, dental, and vision insurance: 61% / 47%
- Work-from-home options: 55% / 40%
- More flexible hours: 47% / 38%
- Unlimited vacation: 47% / 33%
- More vacation time: 40% / 32%
- Paid maternity/paternity leave: 24% / 14%
- Student loan assistance: 24% / 20%
- Free day-care services: 23% / 11%
- Tuition assistance: 16% / 14%
- Free fitness/yoga classes: 11% / 9%
- Free gym membership: 11% / 12%
- Free coffee: 10% / 12%
- Free snacks: 9% / 10%
- Company-wide retreats: 6% / 7%
- Team bonding events: 5% / 7%
- Weekly free employee outings: 5% / 6%
- On-site gym: 4% / 6%
Source: Jones, Kerry. “The Most Desirable Employee Benefits.” Harvard Business Review. Feb 15, 2017. (Some data from FRACTL. “The Cost of Employee Happiness.” http://www.frac.tl/employee-benefits-study/)

DATA:
Categories are horizontal bars comparing percentages for Women (coral/orange bars) and Men (blue bars).
- Better health, dental, and vision insurance: Women 61%, Men 47%
- Work-from-home options: Women 55%, Men 40%
- More flexible hours: Women 47%, Men 38%
- Unlimited vacation: Women 47%, Men 33%
- More vacation time: Women 40%, Men 32%
- Paid maternity/paternity leave: Women 24%, Men 14%
- Student loan assistance: Women 24%, Men 20%
- Free day-care services: Women 23%, Men 11%
- Tuition assistance: Women 16%, Men 14%
- Free fitness/yoga classes: Women 11%, Men 9%
- Free gym membership: Women 11%, Men 12%
- Free coffee: Women 10%, Men 12%
- Free snacks: Women 9%, Men 10%
- Company-wide retreats: Women 6%, Men 7%
- Team bonding events: Women 5%, Men 7%
- Weekly free employee outings: Women 5%, Men 6%
- On-site gym: Women 4%, Men 6%

KEY FACTS:
- "Better health, dental, and vision insurance" is ranked as the most important benefit by both women (61%) and men (47%).
- Women consistently rank healthcare, work-from-home options, flexible hours, and vacation benefits higher than men do.
- The largest percentage gap between genders is for "Free day-care services" (23% of women vs. 11% of men) and "Work-from-home options" (55% of women vs. 40% of men).
- For a few lower-ranked perks—such as free gym membership, free coffee, free snacks, company-wide retreats, team bonding events, weekly free employee outings, and on-site gym—men's percentages slightly exceed or equal women's percentages.
- The least valued benefit overall for women is "On-site gym" at 4%, while for men it is "Free fitness/yoga classes" at 9%.
